title: Grow space setup — controlled evidence plan
purpose: Define a grow-space commissioning and readiness workflow that verifies safe access, utilities, drainage, environmental measurement, cleaning access and equipment status without turning cultivation training into engineering or licensed-trade authority.

excludedUntilQualified: acceptance of a room solely because controller setpoints look correct

claims.statement: Cannabis cultivation work can involve interacting chemical, biological, ergonomic, electrical, equipment and physical hazards, so grow-space setup should begin with a site-specific hazard and workflow assessment rather than only horticultural targets.
claims.boundary: A generic course hazard list cannot replace the employer's actual hazard assessment, emergency plan or qualified engineering review.

claims.statement: Walking and working surfaces should be maintained in a clean, orderly and sufficiently dry condition, making drainage, hose/cable routing and spill control part of cultivation-space readiness.
claims.boundary: This requirement does not authorize unqualified repair of plumbing, electrical or structural defects discovered during inspection.

claims.statement: Damaged powered equipment, defeated safeguards or conditions requiring covered servicing should be removed from normal operation and escalated through the authorized energy-control/maintenance process.
claims.boundary: Taking the cultivation course does not qualify a learner as an authorized electrical, mechanical or lockout/tagout servicing employee.

claims.statement: Environmental measurements are only useful for commissioning when sensor location and exposure are representative of the crop question being asked; one controller sensor can miss canopy-level spatial gradients.
claims.boundary: Measured treatment values in research should not be copied into universal room setpoints for all cultivars and stages.

claims.statement: Temperature and humidity conditions can materially affect cannabis growth, flowering development and metabolite outcomes, supporting verification of actual crop-zone conditions before production begins.
claims.boundary: Commissioning verifies the space against the approved facility crop plan; it does not define a universal cannabis climate recipe.

claims.statement: Space layout should support separation of clean and dirty workflows, routine inspection, sanitation access and safe movement of people, plants, tools and materials.
claims.boundary: Exact aisle widths, equipment spacing and room geometry must follow applicable code, equipment instructions and facility design requirements.

claims.statement: A controller command or displayed status is not the same as verified physical delivery, so commissioning should compare intended operation with observable outputs such as airflow, irrigation/drainage, alarms and representative environmental measurements.
claims.boundary: The cultivation SOP should define verification and escalation, not unauthorized technical adjustment of engineered systems.

claims.statement: Commissioning records should identify the room/zone, equipment or system checked, date/time, required criterion, observed result, unresolved defect, containment and responsible handoff before the area is released for normal use.
claims.boundary: A checklist completion mark does not override an unresolved safety, engineering, sanitation or legal defect.
